subtopics.title: Bond Breaking, Bond Making and the Heat of Reaction

questions.question: Breaking a chemical bond always:
options: Releases energy
Absorbs energy
Leaves the energy unchanged
Releases energy only in exothermic reactions

questions.question: The heat of reaction ΔH is defined as:
options: The energy of the products minus the energy of the reactants
The energy of the reactants minus the energy of the products
The energy at the peak of the graph
The energy released by the surroundings

questions.question: A negative ΔH means that:
options: The surroundings lost energy
The reaction cannot occur
The system (the chemicals) lost energy to the surroundings
The products store more energy than the reactants

questions.question: In a reaction where bond forming releases more energy than bond breaking absorbs:
options: The products end at higher potential energy
ΔH is positive
The surroundings cool down
The surplus energy is released and ΔH is negative

questions.question: Which reaction is endothermic?
options: Combustion of methane
Photosynthesis
Respiration
Neutralisation of an acid by a base

questions.question: During an exothermic reaction, the surroundings:
options: Warm up, because the system releases energy
Cool down, because the system absorbs energy
Stay at exactly the same temperature
First cool down and then warm up

questions.question: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate proceeds only while heat is supplied because:
options: The reaction is exothermic
Calcium carbonate is a catalyst
The products store more energy than the reactants, so energy must be continuously imported
The carbon dioxide escapes too quickly

questions.question: An instant cold pack works because:
options: An exothermic reaction releases cold
The pack contains ice
A catalyst removes heat from the skin
An endothermic dissolution absorbs heat from the surroundings

subtopics.title: Activation Energy and the Activated Complex

questions.question: The activation energy is:
options: The minimum energy colliding particles need in order to react
The difference between reactant and product energies
The energy released when the products form
The energy stored in the catalyst

questions.question: The activated complex is best described as:
options: A stable intermediate product that can be isolated
The unstable transition state of maximum potential energy, with old bonds partly broken and new bonds partly formed
The mixture of reactants before heating
The catalyst-reactant compound

questions.question: A match is needed to start a braai fire because the match:
options: Supplies all the energy the fire will release
Lowers the activation energy of combustion
Acts as a catalyst
Supplies the activation energy for the first molecules, after which the reaction's own energy sustains it

questions.question: Petrol and oxygen can coexist peacefully in a fuel tank because the reaction between them has:
options: A positive ΔH
No activated complex
A high activation energy
A low activation energy

subtopics.title: Potential Energy Graphs, Catalysed and Uncatalysed

questions.question: On a potential energy graph with reactants at 50 kJ, peak at 120 kJ and products at 20 kJ, the activation energy of the forward reaction is:
options: 100 kJ
70 kJ
30 kJ
120 kJ

questions.question: For the same graph, ΔH of the forward reaction is:
options: +30 kJ
−70 kJ
−30 kJ

questions.question: The activation energy of the REVERSE reaction on that graph is:
options: 100 kJ
70 kJ
30 kJ
20 kJ

questions.question: Adding a catalyst changes the graph by:
options: Lowering both the peak and the product level
Raising the reactant level
Lowering ΔH
Lowering the peak only — the reactant and product levels, and therefore ΔH, are unchanged

subtopics.title: Paying to Break, Earning to Build

questions.question: In the magnet picture, pulling two magnets apart is like:
options: Breaking a bond, which costs energy
Forming a bond, which costs energy
Breaking a bond, which releases energy
A catalysed reaction

questions.question: A braai fire is exothermic because:
options: Breaking up the wood releases energy
The new bonds formed in the products pay out more energy than it cost to break the old bonds
The wood absorbs heat from the coals
Oxygen stores heat that the fire sets free

questions.question: ΔH is negative for an exothermic reaction because the sign is attached to:
options: The surroundings, which gained energy
Your hands, which feel the heat
The chemicals, which ended up with less stored energy
The thermometer reading

subtopics.title: The Entry Fee — Why the Braai Needs a Match

questions.question: The "entry fee" in the lesson stands for:
options: The heat of reaction
The energy released by the products
The mass of reactants needed
The activation energy

questions.question: A fire keeps burning after one match because:
options: The match keeps supplying energy
The payout from each reaction covers the entry fee for neighbouring molecules
The activation energy disappears once the fire starts
Oxygen lowers the entry fee over time

questions.question: A fire struggles with wet wood because:
options: Water raises the activation energy of combustion
Water is a catalyst for the reverse reaction
The reaction's payout is spent boiling water instead of funding the next entry fees
Wet wood contains no bonds to break

questions.question: The size of the entry fee (activation energy) tells you:
options: How easily the reaction starts — not how much energy it releases overall
Exactly how much energy the reaction releases
Whether ΔH is positive or negative
How hot the flame will be

subtopics.title: Reading the Hill Between Two Valleys

questions.question: On the hiking-trail picture, the activation energy is:
options: The height difference between the two valleys
The climb from the starting valley up to the ridge
The depth of the destination valley
The length of the trail

questions.question: A trail starting at 50, cresting at 120 and ending at 20 represents a reaction with:
options: Eₐ = 120 kJ and ΔH = +30 kJ
Eₐ = 30 kJ and ΔH = −70 kJ
Eₐ = 70 kJ and ΔH = −30 kJ
Eₐ = 100 kJ and ΔH = −30 kJ

questions.question: Walking the same trail backwards (products to reactants) gives:
options: A climb of 100 and a finish 30 higher than the start
A climb of 70 and a finish 30 lower
No climb at all
The same climb of 70 and the same ΔH

questions.question: A catalyst is like a tunnel through the ridge because it:
options: Moves the destination valley lower
Makes the walk release more energy
Raises the starting valley
Lowers the climb without moving either valley, so the reaction is faster but ΔH is unchanged
